newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends mixed, Dec/March swells to 60 stg.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends mixed, Dec/March swells to 60 stg.

text.p: London's expiring December cocoa contract felt the brunt of Friday's selling pressure as it stood 60 stg cheaper than the following March in closing deals, traders said.

In an otherwise featureless session, the Dec/March switch widened from an earlier 50 stg as players continued to liquidate their spot positions before Monday's first tender. There was little impetus to chase the market beyond its broad range with New York shut for Thanksgiving, traders said.
But benchmark March cocoa and further forward positions clawed some gains in late dealings, securing a higher close.
March ended one stg up at 930 stg a tonne after reaching a low of 924. Its highest was 931.
"It may have been some support from offtake," commented one trader.

The day's turnover reached a strong 9,470 lots but had a high concentration of Dec/March exchanges. December lost 12 stg on the day and its open interest was set to shrink futher from an uncovered total of 3,293 lots on Thursday. A conviction that December cocoa will have a short validity period has been weighing on the spot price.
Technically, the market is said to be unarmed to fight any upside challenges and may remain confined to the 943-910 range for the time being.
Cocoa buyers in Ivory Coast's central regions estimated the country's crop at between 800,000 and 850,000 tonnes for the 1996/97 season, saying their purchases were down by 30 percent.
A stream of forecasts from Ivorian locals has been markedly below the views of analysts in consumer countries. They have initially pegged the crop at about 950,000-1,000,000 tonnes.
Analysts reckon that November arrival figures will provide fresh ammunition to revise or confirm estimates.
